Life at school
A typical school day
8:30
Morning homeroom
9:00
Lessons begin (45–50 minutes each)
12:30
School lunch in the classroom
1:00
Cleaning time, done by the students
3:30
Afternoon homeroom and goodbye
4:00+
Club activities (bukatsu)
放課後
HŌKAGO · AFTER SCHOOL
The day does not end at the last bell
Many students join clubs, and some go to a cram school (juku).
Typical day: times vary by school and level, and elementary days usually end earlier.
Life at school
Students help run the school
給食
KYŪSHOKU · SCHOOL LUNCH
  • Students serve the food to their classmates.
  • Everyone eats together in the classroom.
  • Nutritionists plan the menus.
掃除
OSŌJI · CLEANING TIME
  • Students clean their own classrooms and hallways.
  • Everyone shares the work.
  • It teaches respect for shared spaces.
Lunch and cleaning teach manners, responsibility and nutrition.
Sources: Japan Society (About Japan); Arigato Japan. High school students usually bring their own meals.
Life at school
More than lessons
Club activities
部活
Bukatsu
After-school sports and culture clubs, from baseball to brass bands.
Sports day
運動会
Undōkai
A day of team games, relay races and loud cheering.
Culture festival
文化祭
Bunkasai
Students run stalls, plays and concerts for the school.
School trip
修学旅行
Shūgaku ryokō
A class trip, often to historic places such as Kyoto.
School life is also about teamwork, effort and shared memories.
Common school activities in Japan: availability and format vary by school.
Exam culture
The big test
496,237
applicants for the Common Test for University Admissions
Taken in January 2026 at about 650 venues across Japan.
受験
Juken
Exam preparation, a serious season of life for many students.
塾
Juku
Private cram schools where many students study after school.
共通
Common Test
A national exam, followed by each university's own test.
Source: NIAD (National Center for University Entrance Examinations), applicants for the January 2026 Common Test.

Challenges
Not everything is perfect
671K
Fewer children
Births in 2025 (671,236). The fertility rate was 1.14, so schools are getting smaller.
354K
School absence
Students absent for 30 days or more in FY2024 (353,970), a record concern for schools.
−13
Reading scores
PISA reading fell from 516 to 503. Experts point to screen time.
Sources: Nippon.com and Adnkronos (births 2025); MEXT survey (absences FY2024); OECD (PISA 2025).
